title: Quasi-coherent commutative algebra sheaves on an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Its regular-functions presheaf on $X_{et}$ is a sheaf of commutative rings, whose ring sheaf is the existing structure sheaf. Define commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebra sheaves as the under-category of this sheaf in commutative ring sheaves: their arrows are ring-sheaf maps commuting with the structure maps. Their underlying modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] are the unit modules of the algebra ring sheaves, restricted along the structure morphism, so $r$ acts on $a$ by $\eta(r)a$. Define $QCAlg(X)$ as the full subcategory whose underlying modules are quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Such an algebra is integral, finite, or finitely presented when on every affine etale scheme chart $V\to X$ its structure map $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)\to A(V)$ is respectively integral, finite as a module, or finitely presented as an algebra (a quotient of a polynomial algebra in finitely many variables by a finitely generated ideal).
